summary: This JUnit test checks a method whose only job is printing. It temporarily redirects System.out into an in-memory buffer, calls printStatusToDisplay(), then compares the captured text against the expected line.

lines.text: A ByteArrayOutputStream collects bytes in memory instead of sending them anywhere, which is what makes captured console output inspectable.
System.out is a PrintStream, so replacing it requires building a new PrintStream of your own.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly rather than Assertions.assertEquals(...).
A placeholder standing in for the earlier tests in this class; the book shows only the new one to keep the focus tight.
This annotation is how JUnit discovers the method and runs it as a test.
The thermostat is created at 72 degrees with heating off, which is exactly the state that should report "Idle".
Saving the real System.out first is essential, because the test must be able to put it back afterwards.
From this point on, anything printed with System.out.println lands in the buffer rather than the console.
The call under test goes inside a try so that restoring System.out can be guaranteed even if it throws.
This is the single action being tested; its only observable effect is the text it prints.
A finally block always runs, whether the call succeeded or failed.
Restoring the original stream keeps this test from silently swallowing the output of every test that runs after it.
The expected value includes System.lineSeparator() because println adds a line break, and using the platform separator keeps the test passing on Windows as well as Linux and macOS.
